pit_profile.why: Lowe's: the world's second largest home improvement retailer, 1,748 home improvement stores and outlets in the U.S. with approximately 195 million square feet, serving do-it-yourself, do-it-for-me and professional customers; its sales follow housing turnover and the activity level of home improvement projects (its own 10-K), the franchise does not

theme_watch.reason: Live: Lowe's own FY2024 10-K says 'We face growing competition from online and omnichannel retailers who have a similar product or service offering. Customers are increasingly able to quickly comparison shop and determine real-time product availability and price using digital tools. We will be at a competitive disadvantage if, over time, our competitors are more effective than us in their utilization and integration of rapidly evolving technologies, including AI and machine learning technologies. Further, online and omnichannel retailers continue to focus on delivery services, as customers are increasingly seeking faster, guaranteed delivery times, including same-day and next-day fulfillment, low-price or free shipping, and convenient pick-up options, and we must make investments to keep up with our customers’ evolving shopping preferences.' At the same time it sells online itself: 'For purchases made on Lowes.com, customers may pick up their purchase in-store at the customer service desk, curbside, or from touchless lockers, or have their purchase delivered to their home or business.'. The stock trades at 18.5x FY25E — near its own median. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ECOMMERCE) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing online substitution of Lowe's store sales specifically.

classification.quality_note: Lowe's: the world's second largest home improvement retailer, 1,748 home improvement stores and outlets in the U.S. with approximately 195 million square feet, serving do-it-yourself, do-it-for-me and professional customers; its sales follow housing turnover and the activity level of home improvement projects (its own 10-K), the franchise does not. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 0.83x; +23% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.81; conservative 2yr +10%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -8.4%/yr (worst year FY15-FY24, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +6.4%/yr (FY25 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +15.5%/yr (FY15-FY24 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +44.8%/yr (best 2-yr run FY15-FY24); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: LOW (retrospective, 2025-07-25) ◎ ACCUMULATE — Ratio B 0.83x (33.9% downside to Bear $150 / +40.7% upside to Bull $319) | Adj composite 1.67 vs market 2.48: gap -0.81 [OVERVALUED] | +23% above the EPP floor $184 (15x FY25E $12.28) | Conservative 2-yr case: +10.4% total (+5.2%/yr) | At 18.5x FY25E the 15% hurdle price $300 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; comps -1.7% in Q1 FY25, forward sales -0.2% to +1% (FY25 sales guide); e-commerce competition is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
